Independently enumerated every edge subset of K_{2,2}, K_{2,3}, K_{3,3}, K_{3,4} at every m (totals 16,64,512,4096) to compute rational covariance and compare binomial formula; all exact equalities and zero/negative boundaries passed.

correctness.rationale: For complete bipartite K_{a,b}, uniform choice of exactly m distinct edges, a,b>=2, all joint falling factorial moments of isolated side counts equal (a)_r (b)_s * binom((a-r)(b-s),m)/binom(ab,m) for allowable integer ranges. The conditional pair-event ratio factors into product of 1-rsj/((ab-rb-j)(ab-as-j)), giving strict negative cross-part factorial dependence at m>=2 when both margins are positive. The exact covariance sign interval follows at r=s=1. In the balanced sparse m/n->c>0 the product log expansion gives covariance -> -(c²/2)e^(-2c). With-replacement independent row/column index sequences give independence; Bernoulli edges give covariance ab*p*(1-p)^(a+b-1)>0.
risks: Strict inequality requires 1<=r<a,1<=s<b and positive marginals; when joint event impossible but marginal events possible, inequality still strict.
Factorial-moment cross-part negativity is not full negative association or negative quadrant dependence.

value.rationale: The negative/zero/positive covariance contrast between natural three ways of sampling the same bipartite potential-edge set is a concrete structural probabilistic distinction, with exact all-size factorial moment inequality and nontrivial balanced sparse limit.
